decision.rationale: The integrity and exact-source plumbing is green, but the candidate validators primarily execute factory-generated records or branch on trusted fixture-kind labels. Multiple adversarial calls and schema instances pass without the serialized authority, evidence, cryptographic, temporal, or matrix data required by the amendment. A declared green suite therefore does not establish closure of the security, privacy, accessibility, lifecycle, migration, money, legal, or provider-recovery findings.

findings.title: Protected Exam authorization accepts a version-only manifest

reproduction.observed: ALLOW with credentialAccess=1, installationToken=1, providerRequest=1, and gitWrite=1
reproduction.expected: DENY before every operational effect because denyByDefault, target/path, actor/principal, upstream action, selectors, credential lifetime, delegation, assignment, idempotency, CAS, reservation, and resource policy are absent

findings.analysis: The decision function checks only manifest.version and the caller-supplied fixture kind. It never consumes an immutable serialized request, credential, delegation, assignment, authority record, provider resource, path matcher, idempotency ledger, CAS head, or reservation. Distinct hostile-principal cases are labels that return predetermined errors rather than coherent signed counterexamples.
findings.requiredFix: Implement one schema-validated protected-action decision over caller-supplied serialized manifest, request, upstream/downstream credentials, delegation, assignment, authority, provider resources, replay ledger, CAS head, and reservation. Derive actor and path decisions from those bytes. Add coherent independently resealed originator, platform-agent, worker, Builder, compromised, retry, retry-drift, and fallback records. Reject missing, extra, unknown, malformed, wildcard, zero-match, multi-match, stale, and substituted values before effects, and prove expected-versus-executed record-ID equality.

findings.title: Accessibility validator generates a matrix instead of validating executed evidence

reproduction.mutation: Set checkpointModel to Z99/count 1, requiredRowFields to an empty array, and the win11-chrome-jaws environment values to Linux, Lynx, and no assistive technology while preserving its ID and nonempty version strings
reproduction.observed: accessibilityMatrixProof returned valid=true, rowCount=2664900, with the same digest as the unmodified candidate
reproduction.expected: Registry mismatch and missing required fields must fail

findings.analysis: The function checks the ordered environment IDs and nonempty version strings, then internally fabricates passing rows. It ignores checkpointModel, requiredRowFields, exact environment value tuples, any externally executed raw rows, raw row signatures, summary bytes, and evidence retrieval. For most negative kinds it constructs a local mutated row and returns a hard-coded failure before comparing that row with an expected key set. The reported 2,664,900 rows are loop iterations, not validated human evidence.
findings.requiredFix: Define a closed schema for the accessibility manifest, raw row, signed summary, environment registry, and evidence references. Accept retrieved raw row bytes as input; derive expected keys from the exact bound registry; compare exact missing/extra/duplicate keys; validate every field and environment tuple; verify signatures and evidence hashes; derive N/A and overall decisions. Add independently supplied positive and mutated raw bundles rather than internal generated pass rows.

findings.title: Lifecycle and human-authority schemas and oracles admit unauthenticated or structurally incomplete evidence

reproductions.case: A record-committed event with recordSha256 deleted and the outer record resealed
A RAW-POLICY-GRANT whose nested authority contains every required key but every value is null
reproductions.expected: Reject invalid identity, hat, qualification, time, policy, target, provider proof, inventory, safeguard, and signature values

reproductions.case: A HUMAN-AUTHORITY instance with not-a-time in all temporal fields and non-base64 signature bytes

findings.analysis: The lifecycle schema has no conditional eventType-to-required-members branches. RAW-POLICY-GRANT uses a permissive patternProperties=true wrapper that does not apply the HUMAN-AUTHORITY field constraints. Human temporal fields lack formats and the semantic function does not accept supplied authority/provider bytes; it creates its own fixture pair. Lifecycle providerProofDigest is opaque and never verified against provider proof bytes or an independently selected trust anchor. The human provider proof binds only authority ID, provider record ID, subject, decision, and time, not the target Exam, policy, inventory, conditions, safeguards, or destructive scope.
findings.requiredFix: Use closed conditional schemas for every lifecycle event and compose RAW-POLICY-GRANT with an actual HUMAN-AUTHORITY schema reference. Validate strict RFC3339 ordering/currentness and nonempty identifiers. Consume retrieved signed authority, identity, qualification, assignment, provider-proof, inventory, event-history, replay, and CAS bytes; independently select trust anchors; bind provider proofs to the complete human decision and destructive scope; derive the lifecycle boundary and result from validated histories. Re-run all hostile authority and event cases on serialized inputs.

findings.title: The claimed 3608-row migration matrix does not execute migration evidence or matrix semantics

reproduction.expected: Unknown or incomplete input must fail; interleaving and rollback outcomes must derive from validated plan, cleanup authorization, journal, provider result, backup, restoration, and pre/post truth bytes

findings.analysis: The Cartesian loop creates 3,600 IDs, but migrationDecision receives only an idempotency or interruption label. Version, phase, interleaving, rollback, batches, checkpoints, application compatibility, columns, data, tenants, signatures, truth inventory, provider result, backup, and restoration are never passed or compared. MIGRATION-EVIDENCE is compiled but no instance is validated and no signature is verified. Row count is therefore multiplication, not executed assurance.
findings.requiredFix: Drive every matrix row with a complete serialized MIGRATION-EVIDENCE graph. Validate schemas and all signatures, exact plan and cleanup scope, every batch/checkpoint/interruption, old/new reader/writer result, rollback state, CAS/idempotency, provider result, backup/restoration, and pre/post truth. Reject undeclared dimensions and require exact expected tuple keys equal executed result keys.

findings.title: Spend, forecast, invoice, and reconciliation decisions remain label-driven and unsigned

reproductions.observed: ALLOW without any invoice, authorization, provider acknowledgement, usage, variance, or reconciliation record input
reproductions.expected: Decisions must derive from parsed, signed, cryptographically and semantically validated records

findings.analysis: spendDecision builds unsigned local objects and branches on a trusted kind. It does not parse or verify the existing SPEND-AUTHORIZATION schema record, provider proof, five scope trees, price digest, predecessor signatures, CAS reservation, or consumer record. costDecision receives only a label; invoice/reconciliation allows require no record. The sub-cent control uses Number, not BigInt, and tests only three small constants, so it does not exercise safe-integer or multiplication overflow. The declared vectors cannot prove the amendment's cryptographic, temporal, provider/SKU, lineage, and checked-integer contract.
findings.requiredFix: Accept only serialized signed spend, forecast, reservation, usage, invoice, variance, and reconciliation records; schema-validate and recompute all digests/signatures/provider proofs; traverse and validate the full predecessor chain and CAS/idempotency state; validate all five scopes and provider/SKU/class containment; derive forecast and close timing; use checked BigInt nanoUSD arithmetic including boundary/overflow vectors. Reject unknown kinds before effects.

findings.title: Sanitized-real validation does not consume a closed supplied graph and the detector is not category-complete

reproductions.expected: Reject empty supplied corpus and inventory

samples: My postal address is 42 Oak Lane
I am Alice Example, employed by ExampleCo
reproductions.observed: detectIdentifiers returned an empty array for every sample
reproductions.expected: The revision-bound direct-identifier/free-text policy must detect or deterministically resolve these prohibited categories

findings.analysis: privacyGraphDecision treats its first argument as a fixture-kind label and internally creates the only graph it validates. Source authority/use records, signed provenance, prompt contents, detector outputs, baseline/shrink/derivative inventories, per-copy authorities, receipts, and destination credentials are not supplied as verified bytes. Linkage is not recomputed from a source pool; it compares two hard-coded numbers. The detector registry contains class names and prose normalization only; actual regexes and samples live unbound in code, and each class has only one superficial evasion and one boundary phrase.
findings.requiredFix: Create closed schemas for the complete sanitized-real graph and detector implementation/configuration. Consume manifest-bound prompt bytes, signed provenance/use/inspection/disposition records, complete derivative/copy inventories and destinations; independently recompute detector, NER, unique four-token, k, linkage, and Wilson results from the frozen source pool. Expand deterministic detection and adversarial normalization/category cases, including IPv6 and alternate name/address/self-identification forms.

findings.title: Provider-recovery schema and oracle do not establish the claimed trust-domain proof

reproduction.case: A PROVIDER-RECOVERY object with empty organization, tenant, repository, item, subject, hat, seat, provider/account/export/mapping IDs; not-time timestamps; not-base64 artifact/proof/signature bytes; and arbitrary signature metadata
reproduction.expected: Closed schema rejection before proof evaluation

findings.analysis: The semantic function creates its own recovery record and provider/verifier proofs. The positive path does not verify the outer recovery record signature; that check is conditional on the bad-record-signature fixture label. It does not verify verifier trustAnchorDigest, retrievedEvidenceDigest, or the provider proof's complete identity/decision/policy/lifecycle/export binding. Field mutation cases are rejected by kind after resealing rather than because a validated independent proof contradicts them. No provider key registry artifact is present in this round-three package, so trust selection remains code-local.
findings.requiredFix: Strengthen schema formats and nonempty constraints, add an independently hash-bound provider/verifier key registry, and validate caller-supplied canonical journal/export/restored/verifier bytes. Always verify the outer record, provider proof, and verifier proof; bind all required fields into provider and verifier preimages; independently derive cursor continuity, mapping bijection, Git bytes, and record inventory; reject mutations based on evidence, not fixture labels.

details: executedIds and executedKinds are accumulated but never compared at the end with one complete declared expected-ID/kind set; the final DECLARED_EXECUTION_OK line prints set sizes without an equality assertion.
The authorization loop iterates whatever rows are present; namedHostilePaths is compared separately to a constant but fixture authorization kind/ID completeness is not compared to it.
The accessibility loop marks one positive fixture ID and 21 negative IDs, not 2,664,900 externally executed raw row keys.
The migration loop marks 3,600 distinct string IDs while the oracle receives only one derived kind and ignores version, phase, interleaving, and rollback.
Several schema files are compiled but PROVIDER-RECOVERY, RAW-POLICY-GRANT, and MIGRATION-EVIDENCE receive no positive instance validation in the validator.
declaredVsExecutedAudit.requiredFix: Publish one canonical expected execution-key inventory derived from closed fixture schemas, record every actually consumed serialized input/result key, and assert exact equality, uniqueness, and no undeclared rows. Counts alone must not satisfy completeness.
